belay.4: On a small ledge at the old belay where the Thin Red Line pendulum begins; clip the older bolt to the left and back it up to the better anchor on the right.
belay.6: On a good ledge, with the anchor about 25 ft to the right, level with the seventh pitch of the neighbouring Thin Red Line.
belay.11: At a fixed three-nut anchor just above the trees, reached by wandering onto lower-angle ground after the finger-crack corner.

belay.P8: A full rope length up from the base of the steep wall that the blocky ramp cuts through.
belay.P9: On the large ledge that tops the first 5.9 pitch.

belay.1: On a comfortable ledge on top of the lowest pillar, at the end of the hand crack.
belay.2: Inside the wide crack that splits the lower buttress, after traversing the face leftward.
belay.3: On a pedestal at the top of the pillar, under a large diving-board block, with medium nuts for protection.
belay.4: Among blocks near the middle of the buttress, once the crack ends and the ground turns blocky.
belay.5: Directly under the block that caps the corner crack and forms a keyhole.
belay.6: Out on the bivy ledge used by the first ascent party, above the chimney system.
belay.7: At the base of the upper headwall; on a 60 m rope stop short and scramble about 10 m of easy third class to reach it.
belay.8: On a ledge with an old, doubtful angle piton; a #6 cam is convenient, otherwise use small gear and chockstones.
belay.9: In a corner among large blocks, above the vertical hand crack.
